---
title: "05b — Physical versus social-predictor signal"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** whether physical-health indicators, social/demographic indicators, or their combination improve **2023 out-of-time classification** over the simple historical prevalence baseline. This exploratory analysis uses logistic regression with different sets of predictors. It does not determine causation or change the frozen national model selection.

## Setup

Loads the same run increment as the main model. The 2025 survey is not opened or scored
in this notebook.

```{r setup}
# Find the open RStudio project root and load shared R Notebook modules.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```

## Compare predictor groups

Each logistic regression is fitted on 2014–2022 and assessed on 2023 with the same
weighting and survey outcome definition. These are **associational predictors**;
differences do not identify causal social determinants.

```{r compare-predictor-groups}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Predictor-group comparison
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep training and evaluation years fixed while changing the predictor set.
# These logistic comparisons describe predictive association, not causal effects.

training <- as.data.frame(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_development"))
validation <- as.data.frame(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_selection_2023"))
training$.model_weight <- normalize_weights(training$train_weight)

predictor_groups <- list(
    physical_only = c("physical_days_group", "general_health_group"),
    social_demographic_only = c("AGE_BAND", "SEX_CLEAN", "EDU_CLEAN", "INCOME_BAND"),
    combined = feature_names
)

rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (group_name in names(predictor_groups)) {
    formula <- stats::reformulate(predictor_groups[[group_name]], response = "FMD")
    model <- suppressWarnings(stats::glm(
        formula,
        data = training,
        family = stats::binomial(),
        weights = .model_weight,
        control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 60)
    ))
    if (!isTRUE(model$converged)) {
        stop("Ablation logistic model did not converge: ", group_name)
    }
    prediction <- stats::predict(model, newdata = validation, type = "response")
    rows[[group_name]] <- data.frame(
        predictor_group = group_name,
        weighted_metrics(validation$FMD, prediction, validation$RAW_WEIGHT)
    )
}

historical_average <- weighted_mean(training$FMD, training$train_weight)
rows[["historical_average"]] <- data.frame(
    predictor_group = "historical_average",
    weighted_metrics(
        validation$FMD,
        rep(historical_average, nrow(validation)),
        validation$RAW_WEIGHT
    )
)
results <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)[order(brier)]

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(results, "05b_2023_feature_group_comparison")
print(results)
```

## Visualize added predictive value

The graph displays the 2023 Brier score for each group of predictors. A physical-health
signal may be strong because the predictors and FMD outcome are reported at the same
time; **do not interpret this as prediction of future individual health or as a causal
effect**.

```{r visualize-predictor-groups}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Predictor-group probability error
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare 2023 weighted errors on a common scale.
# This exploratory display does not replace the frozen national model selection.


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    results,
    ggplot2::aes(reorder(predictor_group, brier), brier, fill = predictor_group)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    atg_scale_fill_predictor_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "How much do physical versus social predictors add?",
        subtitle = "2023 survey-weighted Brier score after 2014–2022 training",
        x = "Predictor group",
        y = "Brier score (lower is better)"
    )
show_and_save(plot, "05b_predictor_group_brier", 10, 5)
```
